# SK2011 — A struct uses inherited ValueType.Equals

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A call on a concrete struct binds to System.ValueType.Equals(object) instead of a typed or overridden equality method.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

The inherited implementation uses object-based fallback comparison and can require boxing. Implementing a deliberate equality contract gives collections and direct comparisons a consistent typed path.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
struct Point { public int X; } // point.Equals(other) binds to ValueType.Equals
```

Write:

```csharp
struct Point : IEquatable<Point> { public int X; public bool Equals(Point other) => X == other.X; public override bool Equals(object? other) => other is Point point && Equals(point); public override int GetHashCode() => X; }
```

## When it does not fire

The bound target must be the inherited ValueType.Equals member and the receiver must be a concrete struct. Typed overloads, overrides, records, enums, nullable values and already-boxed receivers are excluded. No fix generates equality or changes comparisons without knowing which fields define identity.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2011.severity`
